profile.summary: A clinical comparison of two metagenomic workflows for detecting microbes in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid: short-read sequencing on MGI and host-depleted nanopore sequencing (HD-ONT). On 62 BALF specimens, each workflow's organism calls are scored against culture, clinical microbiological tests and a composite reference standard by positive and negative percent agreement. It is for clinical microbiology labs weighing short-read against rapid nanopore metagenomics for pneumonia diagnostics.

Clinical validation was conducted on 62 BALF samples. Diagnostic performance was assessed against culture, clinical microbiological tests (CMT), and a composite reference standard (CRS).

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: Whether each sequencing workflow finds the organisms that reference methods find in a patient's BALF, and how many extra organisms it reports. The paper also studies mock communities, but the store's protocols cover only the 62 clinical specimens.

quotes.text: This study aimed to compare the analytical characteristics and diagnostic performance of short-read next-generation sequencing (NGS) and long-read third-generation sequencing (TGS) for metagenomic pathogen detection, using defined mock communities and clinical bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) samples.
Mock evaluations included microbe-host gradient mixtures (D1/D2) and six complex microbial panels (M1–M6).
Clinical validation was conducted on 62 BALF samples. Diagnostic performance was assessed against culture, clinical microbiological tests (CMT), and a composite reference standard (CRS).

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: Residual BALF specimens with traceable culture results were sequenced with the MGI short-read workflow (MGISEQ-200, single-end 50 bp) and the HD-ONT workflow (nuclease and saponin host depletion, GridION R9.4.1). Reads were host-filtered against GRCh38 and classified against a curated database of 20,484 genomes or sequences. A species was called when normalised reads passed RP20M of at least 3 (short read) or RP10K of at least 1 (HD-ONT).

quotes.text: Residual BALF specimens with traceable culture results were selected and stored at
sequenced on the MGISEQ-200 platform (single-end 50 bp).
Libraries were constructed with the Rapid PCR Barcoding Kit (SQK-RPB004, Oxford Nanopore Technologies) and sequenced on GridION X5 instruments using R9.4.1 flow cells.
Host reads were removed by aligning cleaned reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38) together with a plasmid sequence collection.
The final database comprised 20,484 reference genomes/sequences in total, including 5,742 bacteria, 600 fungi, 13,786 viruses, 170 archaea, and 186 parasites/protozoa.
A species was considered positive when the normalized read count exceeded the predefined platform-specific threshold, namely RP20M ≥ 3 for short-read workflows and RP10K ≥ 1 for HD-ONT.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: Each workflow's organism calls are compared with three references: routine culture; clinical microbiological tests (culture plus qPCR or GeneXpert verification where residual volume allowed); and a composite reference standard that adds organisms detected by both sequencing workflows. Agreement is assessed per organism and summarised as PPA and NPA, restricted to bacteria and fungi. Against the composite standard, the paper reports PPA of 93.3% (NGS) and 90.7% (TGS), and NPA of 77.6% and 83.3%.

quotes.text: For clinical specimens, results obtained from the MGI and HD-ONT workflows were evaluated against three comparators:
Routine culture, which included only microorganisms that can be cultured.
Clinical microbiological tests (CMT), integrating results from culture and additional verification.

Composite reference standard (CRS), which incorporated organisms that lacked targeted testing results but were consistently detected by both sequencing workflows (MGI and HD-ONT) under the predefined reporting criteria.
These targeted assays were used as part of the CMT comparator framework for confirmatory evaluation rather than to serve as an error-free gold standard.
were verified by quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) using published primer sets specific to the target organisms.
Agreement between each sequencing workflow and each comparator was assessed at the organism level.
positive percent agreement (PPA) and negative percent agreement (NPA) were calculated accordingly.
Therefore, we restricted the formal performance analyses (PPA/NPA) to bacterial and fungal pathogens.

In clinical specimens, when evaluated against the composite reference standard, the positive percent agreement (PPA) values of NGS and TGS were 93.3% and 90.7%, respectively, with corresponding negative percent agreements (NPAs) of 77.6% and 83.3%.
